engine.label: Pocket TTS 18M · bill_boerst
engine.streaming: native incremental: generate_audio_stream, 12.5 Hz latents decoded by Mimi as queued
engine.chunkPolicy: upstream: text split at sentences into chunks of at most 50 tokens; each yield is one Mimi decode of every queued 80 ms frame (1920 samples each), so the first chunk is one frame
engine.cancellation: stop event before every latent frame (80 ms of audio) and every text chunk; queued frames still decode

loadDetail.note: loadMs is torch and pocket_tts import, load_model on the local config, and the bill_boerst voice state from its safetensors

Here is where things stand on the release. The migration ran overnight and finished without errors, so the new tables are live in staging. If you are happy with that plan, I will schedule the production rollout for Friday morning, before the team meeting. Let me know if you would rather wait until next week, and I will move everything back.

I finished reading the three papers you flagged last night. The first one claims a forty percent speed up, but only on short prompts, and their test machine had twice our memory. The second paper is more useful: it shows that splitting text at commas cuts the wait before speech by about half. The third is mostly a survey, so I only kept the summary table. Overall, I think the comma trick is worth trying first, because it needs no new model and could ship in a day. I wrote up the details in the research folder, with links to each paper and the numbers I checked. Tell me if you want a shorter version for the team update on Monday.
